headline: Stochastic models link population structure, network reduction, and tumor evolution
label: Stochastic Modeling Of Biological Systems
summary: Four June 2026 items add analytical and computational frameworks for reducing stochastic biological dynamics to interpretable low-dimensional descriptions.
synthesis: The dominant thread is stochastic modeling of biological dynamics through reduced or coarse-grained formulations. One preprint reduces mutant fixation in fragmented populations to a low-dimensional Markov chain, with explicit fixation probability and fixation time formulas. Another introduces a scale-splitting, renormalization-inspired algorithm that coarse-grains large chemical reaction networks into effective, interpretable graphs. A third examines how population heterogeneity shapes the redundancy principle, where extreme value statistics govern responses that depend on the fastest few of many searchers. The published PCBI framework models tumor evolution stochastically, linking genotype inheritance, phenotype-driven traits, and resource competition, with a simulation algorithm connected to real data. The common contribution is interpretable reduction of high-dimensional stochastic systems, with explicit analytic results in some items and simulation-based modeling in the cancer framework.
